images.caption: Figure 1:Example of non-Markovian task.Due to architectural limitation, a vanilla VLA loses track after pressing the red button and presses it again. HeLM successfully executes the task by storing progress in language memory, allowing the HLP to guide the LLP correctly.

Figure 3:Update / Detect mode of HLP in evaluation loop.An example of transitions between Detect and Update modes and corresponding memory updates across intra- and inter-episode scenarios. Each actionata_{t}is generated based onMt−1M_{t-1}and the current instruction.

Figure 4:The Real-World Evaluation Suite of HeLM.Our tasks are categorized into two types based on their temporal memory requirements. (Top) Intra-episode tasks (A1–A5) evaluate working memory within a single instruction. (Bottom) Inter-episode tasks (E1–E5) assess episodic context across task boundaries.
Figure 7:Generation of HeLM data.Instead of recording multiple episodes of long-horizon non-Markovian tasks, we use a task configuration list to logically stitch together short subtask episodes.
Figure 8:Four Types of Failure Cases.Examples of low-level, detection, order, and termination failures.
Figure 11:Breakdown of non-Markovian task.Intra-tasks (A1–A5) and Inter-tasks (E1–E5).

Figure 14:Example of HeLM HLP train data.It contains example of HLP training data of HeLM (Press the button N times). There are four types of train data: detect(false), detect(true), update(intra), and update(inter).
